summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Growth vs. IDCW mutual fund plans, but some specific tax rates and exemption limits mentioned are outdated or slightly inaccurate based on recent budget changes.

claims.claim: IDCW stands for 'Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal'. This nomenclature clarifies that the payouts are not solely from 'dividends' earned by the underlying stocks.
claims.note: SEBI renamed dividend option plans to IDCW option plans (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) to clarify that payouts are not solely from dividends and can include capital appreciation or even a portion of the invested capital.

claims.claim: For equity-oriented mutual fund units held for less than one year, gains are taxed at 15% (plus cess and surcharge).
claims.note: As per the Union Budget 2024, for transactions made on or after July 23, 2024, Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) on equity-oriented mutual funds held for less than 12 months are taxed at 20%.

claims.claim: For equity-oriented mutual fund units held for more than one year, LTCG up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year is exempt from tax. Gains exceeding ₹1 lakh are taxed at 10% (plus cess and surcharge) without indexation benefit.
claims.note: As per the Union Budget 2024, for equity-oriented mutual funds, Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) exceeding ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year are taxed at 12.5% (plus cess and surcharge) without indexation benefit, for transactions made on or after July 23, 2024.

claims.claim: For debt-oriented funds, if held for less than three years, gains are added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab.
claims.note: For debt funds, if held for less than 36 months, gains are treated as Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) and are added to the investor's total income and taxed at their slab rate.

claims.claim: For debt-oriented funds held for more than three years, gains are taxed at 20% with the benefit of indexation.
claims.note: For debt mutual funds purchased on or after April 1, 2023, all gains, regardless of the holding period, are added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rate, with no indexation benefit. The old rules (20% with indexation for holdings over 3 years) apply only to investments made before April 1, 2023.

claims.claim: As per current income tax laws, IDCW payouts from all types of mutual funds (equity, debt, hybrid, etc.) are now fully taxable in the hands of the investor. These payouts are treated as 'Income from Other Sources' and are added to your total income. They are then taxed as per your individual income tax slab rate.
claims.note: Since April 1, 2020, IDCW payouts from mutual funds are fully taxable in the hands of the investor as 'Income from Other Sources' and are taxed at their individual income tax slab rate.

claims.claim: Mutual funds are also required to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at the rate of 10% if the IDCW payout exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year.
claims.note: While TDS at 10% is applicable on IDCW payouts, the threshold for deduction has been increased from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 in a financial year, effective from FY 2025-26 (April 1, 2025).

article_title: Mutual Fund Growth vs. IDCW: Understanding Returns & NAV
